solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Diet for a group of owls

definitions.meaning: a diet is a legislative assembly, as in the Japanese Diet
the collective noun for owls, a whimsical term of venery

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a flock of owls eats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diet' poses as food; it is the formal name for a national assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are synonyms: a national legislature is called a Diet in some countries, and owls gather in a group with that collective name.

clue.text: Doctor has boil to remove

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A physician treats a patient's boil by cutting it away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is not a link word here; its letters join those of 'boil' as the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To get rid of a law or practice entirely is to do away with it, a direct synonym of remove.

clue.text: French composer — calm one

parts.note: a lull is a calm spell
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A description of a serene French musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste Lully, also spelt Lulli, was the Italian-born court composer to Louis XIV.

clue.text: Impenetrable expression by drunk

parts.note: an air is a look or manner one expresses, as in an air of confidence
tight is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: A drunk's words are so slurred that nobody can make them out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sealed so nothing can get in or out is impenetrable, the literal sense of sealed against gas.

clue.text: One might go on before one goes off

definitions.text: One might go on before one goes off

parts.words: One might go on before one goes off
parts.note: a bed warmer is switched on before the sleeper drifts off to sleep

explanation.surface: It sounds like a riddle about an act going on stage before another leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes on' is being switched on; 'goes off' is the sleeper falling asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated bed cover is turned on to warm the bed before its owner nods off for the night.

clue.text: Work with hospital in attempt to get prize

indicators.note: in says the work and hospital letters sit inside the word for attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
OP is short for opus, a work
H is the abbreviation for hospital on maps and signs

explanation.surface: A patient recovering in hospital tries hard to win an award.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup or statuette awarded to a winner is a prize, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Flipping poet's boring

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it around, so the word for poet is read backwards

parts.note: a bard is a poet; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: An exasperated reader complains that a poet is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive; it is the reversal signal. 'Flipping' turns BARD into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and lacking colour or interest, so dreary or boring is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Drive with golf club? That's in the water, probably

parts.note: drift can mean to drive or carry along, as wind drives snow into a heap
a wood is a type of golf club used for long shots

explanation.surface: A golfer's drive with a wooden club ends up in the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture makes 'Drive' look like a tee shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Timber washed along by the sea or a river is typically found floating in the water, hence the hedged definition.

clue.text: Notice a soldier — time to be firm

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
a man is a soldier, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A soldier spots a sign telling him it is time to stand firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unshakeable in their opinion is resolute and firm, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Extremely large instrument

parts.note: too means excessively or extremely
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on an enormous musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement used to carry out a task is an instrument, as with surgical instruments.

clue.text: Over-elaborate start to reforms, ethical or otherwise

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so take only the opening letter of reforms
otherwise means in a different way, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A sceptic says the first stage of reforms is ethical or merely so in name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' gives the R of 'reforms'; 'otherwise' rearranges R + ETHICAL + OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Language that is showy and grandiloquent, aiming at effect over substance, is over-elaborate.

clue.text: Cycling with bottom falling off one's swimming costume

indicators.note: in a horizontal light the bottom is the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: biking is cycling
I is the Roman numeral for one; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A cyclist's swimsuit slips down as they ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with bottom falling off' cuts the last letter, leaving BIKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-piece swimsuit worn by women on the beach is a kind of swimming costume.

clue.text: Artist embracing a hot islander

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the painter's name wraps the other letters

parts.note: Titian was the Venetian Renaissance painter
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: A painter hugs a warm-blooded native of a sunny island.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Gauguin painted Tahitians, though the artist here is Titian.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Pacific island of Tahiti is an islander from French Polynesia.

clue.text: Place in China to force someone on board a ship

definitions.meaning: a major port city on China's east coast

definitions.text: to force someone on board a ship
definitions.meaning: to kidnap a man and press him into service as a sailor, an old practice

explanation.surface: A city name sits beside a description of crimping sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: The city lent its name to the verb because sailors were once forcibly conscripted for voyages to the Far East.

clue.text: Surely no savage boxes very timidly?

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the rearranged letters surround the letter for very
to savage something is to maul it, so these letters are torn into a new order

explanation.surface: A question wondering whether a fierce boxer could really fight so shyly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'savage' and 'boxes' both play on the boxing picture; the first yields NEROUSLY, which the second wraps round the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with anxiety and apprehension means behaving shyly, so the adverbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Reluctant to ignore Latin appeal to god

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the Latin letter is dropped

parts.note: loath means unwilling or reluctant

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to bother with a Latin prayer to the deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A solemn promise calls on a deity as witness, so a sworn vow is an appeal to god.

clue.text: Awful noise — car's design

indicators.note: awful suggests something mangled and bad, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written without the possessive, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A car designer is told the engine makes a dreadful racket.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline plan of how events will unfold is a design or scheme for what happens.

clue.text: Fish is after a jelly

indicators.note: after says the fish word comes behind the single letter

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish comes after a wobbly dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatinous substance made from seaweed, used to grow bacteria and to set food, is a jelly.

clue.text: Evil cause of problems affecting Merlin wing, ultimately?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of wing
affecting means acting upon and changing, so the letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: A wicked force is blamed for trouble with Merlin, perhaps a Merlin aircraft's wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives G from 'wing'; 'affecting' rearranges MERLIN + G.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen in the Second World War blamed mechanical faults on a mischievous imp, the classic evil cause of problems.

clue.text: Collapse after second scene

indicators.note: after says the collapse word follows the second word

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
to drop is to collapse

explanation.surface: Someone collapses after an instant, or after the second act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like a unit of time or a rank; it is a verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: The painted cloth hung behind a stage sets the scene, so a background setting is a scene.

clue.text: German sitting on fellow's chest

indicators.note: in a down light, sitting on puts the German name above the fellow

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name
a man is a fellow; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A German man sits on another man's chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chest' looks like a body part; it is a storage box.
explanation.definitionFit: A low upholstered seat with a storage compartment inside doubles as a chest for blankets.

clue.text: Naughty hint about mother: he might take her out

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the mother word
naughty means misbehaving, so the letters are rearranged out of line

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone drops a cheeky hint about mother, suggesting a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take her out' sounds like a date; it means kill. 'Naughty' yields HITN, which 'about' wraps round the parent.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract killer takes victims out, slang for killing, so the definition is a playful example.

clue.text: Cooked sole, main food

indicators.note: cooked suggests ingredients mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A menu note says sole was prepared as the main course.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheat meal used for puddings and pasta is a foodstuff, so food is its general class.

clue.text: Deny information's returned and put away

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for information is read backwards

parts.note: gen is informal for information; the 's stands for 'is'
to put food away is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: Someone denies that information was given back and filed away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' means eaten, not stored. 'returned' turns GEN into NEG.
explanation.definitionFit: To nullify or contradict something is to deny it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Queen absorbed by nerd's language

indicators.note: absorbed by means taken inside, so the queen letter goes into the nerd word

parts.note: a geek is a nerd
R stands for regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A nerd becomes absorbed in studying a queen's tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue spoken in Greece and Cyprus is a language, so this is an example of the class.

clue.text: Skilled worker ordering large masks

indicators.note: ordering means putting into a new sequence, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the fodder
taken as written, part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A craftsman puts in an order for big masks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordering' looks like placing a purchase; it signals rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who blows or moulds glass is an example of a skilled worker.

clue.text: Novel heroine's problem? Matchmaking, to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A literary heroine's flaw is her meddling as a matchmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Jane Austen's heroine famously meddles in matchmaking, so the surface describes her too.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's novel is named after its heroine, Miss Woodhouse, whose matchmaking drives the plot.

clue.text: Resent leaders in Europe now voting "yes"

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so take the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Bitterness over Europe now voting in favour of something.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge another's advantage is to covet it, so the verb is a synonym of resent.

clue.text: Clear on forming business contacts

parts.note: to clear a profit is to net it
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone is clear about building up business connections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' looks like a link word; it means functioning.
explanation.definitionFit: Meeting people to build useful professional relationships is the activity of forming business contacts.
